title: Heartbeats double number line
observableEvidence: Completes several labeled positions on the second line of a double number line from a stated ratio that is not a unit rate.
prompt: A resting heart beats at a steady rate of 12 beats every 10 seconds. On the double number line, the top line shows seconds with marks at 0, 10, 25, 40 and 55. The bottom line shows heartbeats: 0 is below 0 seconds and 12 is below 10 seconds. Box A is below 25 seconds, box B is below 40 seconds and box C is below 55 seconds. Find the number of heartbeats for each box.
solutionRepresentation: 12 beats in 10 seconds is 6 beats in 5 seconds. 25 seconds is 5 groups of 5 seconds, so A = 5 × 6 = 30. 40 seconds is 8 groups, so B = 48. 55 seconds is 11 groups, so C = 66.
solutionMethod: Scale the stated pair down to a value that divides every top mark, then multiply both numbers by the same factor for each box.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: Heartbeats in box A (25 seconds): 30 beats; Heartbeats in box B (40 seconds): 48 beats; Heartbeats in box C (55 seconds): 66 beats
acceptedAnswers: Heartbeats in box A (25 seconds): 30 beats; Heartbeats in box B (40 seconds): 48 beats; Heartbeats in box C (55 seconds): 66 beats
deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Structured whole-number fields, one per labeled box. All three must be correct; no partial credit.

hintSteps.prompt: Not every top mark is a whole number of 10-second groups, so look for a smaller group that fits all of them.
hintSteps.question: What smaller number of seconds divides 25, 40 and 55 evenly?

hintSteps.prompt: Halve both numbers of the stated pair to get the beats for that smaller group, then multiply by how many groups fit in each box's seconds.
hintSteps.question: How many of those smaller groups are in 25 seconds?

hintSteps.prompt: A different example: 9 laps every 6 minutes is 3 laps every 2 minutes, so 14 minutes (7 groups of 2) gives 21 laps.
hintSteps.question: Do all three boxes keep the same beats-to-seconds relationship as 12 to 10?
